llm.summary: This code-refinement skill is mostly aligned with code-quality work, but it includes under-disclosed external posting and unsafe execution guidance that users should review before installing.

dimensions.detail: Read/search commands are proportionate for code review, but the GitHub Discussions publishing flow crosses a network/publication boundary without clear consent, destination validation, or redaction requirements.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact is Markdown-only with no installer, executable package, dependency lockfile, or bundled binary code; referenced integrations depend on external/local plugins and scripts.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The main workflow defaults to plan-only for unqualified use, but execution mode can apply fixes, override scope guards, suppress mid-task check-ins, and resume after harness stop signals when certain phrases are present.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No system persistence or privilege escalation is installed, but the skill instructs continued execution after stop signals and can record closure commits and synthesis files during execution mode.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Local code analysis and optional fix execution fit a code-refinement purpose, but the insight-generation module adds publication of findings to GitHub Discussions, including evidence and recommendations, which is not clearly surfaced in the main skill description.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you want a code-quality skill that may perform broad repository analysis and, when explicitly invoked, modify files. Do not use the insight-generation module on private or sensitive repositories unless you first add an explicit approval, redaction, and destination check for GitHub posting, and avoid the scope-guard and stop-signal override behavior.
llm.findings:
[SDI-1] expected: Optional repository modification is partly expected for code refinement, and the execution table requires explicit phrases such as apply fixes or execute findings; the concern is downgraded to disclosure/scoping rather than purpose incompatibility.
[SSD-4] unexpected: The artifact-backed instructions to avoid mid-run summaries and resume after harness stop signals are not necessary for code refinement and materially weaken user or harness control.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Broad triggers such as craft and algorithms could activate a repository-wide quality workflow in contexts where the user did not clearly request it.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Execution behavior and external publication are disclosed only in deeper workflow/module text, not prominently in the top-level description or quick start.
[SSD-1] unexpected: The ignore scope guard mode explicitly bypasses branch-size limits and allows continued execution past normal containment checks.
[other] unexpected: The GitHub Discussions posting module can publish code-analysis evidence, file references, summaries, and recommendations externally without an explicit preview, consent gate, or redaction step.
[T09] unexpected: The posting snippet interpolates finding fields into a python3 -c program, so repository-derived text containing quotes or code-like payloads could alter executable Python if substituted literally.
